Summary: A 36-year-old woman readmitted three days after discharge for lymphocytic meningitis presents with recurrent severe orthostatic headache, photophobia, upper-limb tremor, and dizziness, with persistent CSF pleocytosis despite clinical improvement.

Working explanations:

Post-dural puncture headache: The orthostatic quality and temporal relationship to the lumbar puncture performed during the first admission strongly support this. Limitation: tremor and dizziness are atypical for simple PDPH, and persistent pleocytosis is unexplained by a mechanical leak alone. Useful next information: opening pressure on repeat LP (not reported).

Persistent or relapsing lymphocytic meningitis: Repeat CSF shows 178 cells/µL with 97.7% lymphocytes, indicating ongoing meningeal inflammation. The original aetiology remains unclear, as she received dexamethasone alone without antivirals or antibiotics. Limitation: protein has decreased (83.3 to 36.6 mg/dL), suggesting partial improvement. Useful next information: aetiological workup (viral PCR, autoimmune panels) and opening pressure.

Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: Meningitis is a recognised risk factor; tremor and dizziness could reflect venous congestion. Limitation: a normal brain MRI does not exclude CVST without dedicated MRV. Useful next information: MR venography.

Reassessment needed: Focused neurological examination for cerebellar or focal signs, and confirmation of opening pressure before committing to management.
